paraphrase: Prince Mahāsattva, seeing a starving tigress about to eat her cubs, gives his own body to her; he was a past life of the Buddha.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked). Narrative of bodily self-giving; not an instruction (restricted category).

paraphrase: The Buddha's lifespan is immeasurable; he entered parinirvāṇa only to ripen beings — the Buddha does not truly pass away, the dharma does not disappear.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: The confession (deśanā) heard from a golden drum seen in a dream: confessing before the buddhas all evil done through ignorance, passion and pride, in this and past lives, and rejoicing in all merit, removes evil karma.
